lessons.title: Introduction to Java and the JVM
lessons.description: Understand Java, the JDK, JRE, JVM and the execution process.
lessons.content:
Java is a high-level, class-based programming language widely used for backend, enterprise and Android-related development.

Java source files use the .java extension. The Java compiler converts source code into bytecode stored in .class files. The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) executes the bytecode.

JDK: Java Development Kit, containing development tools such as javac.
JRE: Java Runtime Environment, providing components needed to run Java programs.
JVM: Java Virtual Machine, responsible for executing Java bytecode.

Java supports object-oriented programming, automatic memory management, exception handling and multithreading.

A typical program begins execution in the main method: public static void main(String[] args).

lessons.title: Variables, Data Types and Operators
lessons.description: Learn Java primitive types, variables, casting and operators.
lessons.content:
A variable stores a value that can be used by a program. Java is statically typed, so each variable has a declared type.

The eight primitive types are byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean.

Reference types include String, arrays and objects.

Arithmetic operators: +, -, *, / and %.
Comparison operators: ==, !=, >, <, >= and <=.
Logical operators: &&, || and !.
Assignment operators: =, +=, -= and others.

Integer division removes the fractional part. For example, 7 / 2 produces 3 when both operands are integers.

Widening conversions are generally automatic; narrowing conversions require explicit casting.

lessons.title: Conditional Statements and Loops
lessons.description: Control program execution using decisions and repetition.
lessons.content:
Control flow statements determine which instructions execute.

if executes code when a condition is true. else handles the alternative. else if supports additional conditions.

switch selects among multiple cases and is useful for menu-based programs.

for loops are useful when the number of iterations is known.
while loops repeat while a condition remains true.
do-while loops execute their body at least once.

break exits a loop or switch. continue skips to the next loop iteration.

Avoid infinite loops by ensuring the loop condition can eventually become false.

lessons.title: Methods, Arrays and Strings
lessons.description: Learn reusable methods and fundamental data structures.
lessons.content:
A method groups reusable instructions and may accept parameters and return a value.

Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists.

An array stores a fixed number of elements of the same type. Array indices begin at zero.

String represents text and is immutable in Java. Operations such as toUpperCase() return a new String rather than changing the original.

Use equals() to compare String content. The == operator compares references for objects.

StringBuilder is useful when text must be modified repeatedly.

lessons.title: Classes, Objects and Java Program Structure
lessons.description: Understand the basics of object-oriented Java programs.
lessons.content:
A class defines fields and methods. An object is an instance of a class.

A constructor initializes a newly created object. Constructors have the same name as the class and do not declare a return type.

The new keyword creates an object.

Instance fields belong to objects, while static fields belong to the class.

Access modifiers such as public and private control visibility.

Packages organize related classes, and import statements allow convenient use of classes from other packages.

Encapsulation commonly uses private fields and public methods to control access.

quizzes.question: Which component executes Java bytecode?
quizzes.explanation: The JVM executes Java bytecode. The compiler converts Java source code into bytecode.

quizzes.question: Which method is the standard entry point of a Java application?
quizzes.explanation: The JVM starts a standard Java application by invoking the main method with the required signature.

quizzes.question: Which of the following is not a primitive Java data type?
quizzes.explanation: String is a reference type. Java has eight primitive types, including int, double and boolean.

quizzes.question: What is the output of System.out.println(7 / 2);?
quizzes.explanation: Both operands are integers, so Java performs integer division and discards the fractional part.

quizzes.question: Which operator performs logical AND with short-circuit evaluation?
quizzes.explanation: The && operator evaluates the right operand only when the left operand is true.

quizzes.question: Which loop executes its body at least once?
quizzes.explanation: A do-while loop evaluates its condition after executing the loop body.

quizzes.question: What is the first valid index of a Java array?
quizzes.explanation: Java arrays use zero-based indexing. The first element is accessed using index 0.

quizzes.question: Which method should generally be used to compare the contents of two Strings?
quizzes.explanation: equals() compares String content, whereas == compares object references.

quizzes.question: What does the new keyword do when creating an object?
quizzes.explanation: The new keyword creates an object instance and invokes the selected constructor.

quizzes.question: Which statement about Java method overloading is correct?
options: Only the return type must change
Methods share a name but have different parameter lists
Overloading is not supported in Java
quizzes.explanation: Method overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists. Changing only the return type is insufficient.

exercises.title: Write Your First Java Program
exercises.description: Create and execute a Java Hello World program.
exercises.instructions: Create a Main class containing public static void main(String[] args). Print Hello, Placify! to the console. Explain what javac and the JVM do.

exercises.title: Build a Simple Calculator
exercises.description: Practice arithmetic operators and user input.
exercises.instructions: Write a Java program that accepts two numbers and an operator (+, -, *, /). Use Scanner to read input and a switch statement to perform the operation. Handle division by zero.

exercises.title: Find the Largest Number in an Array
exercises.description: Practice arrays, loops and conditional statements.
exercises.instructions: Create an integer array containing at least five numbers. Use a loop to find and print the largest value without using Arrays.sort(). Test the program with positive and negative numbers.

exercises.title: Create a Student Grade Calculator
exercises.description: Use methods, arrays and conditional statements.
exercises.instructions: Write a Java program that stores marks for five subjects, calculates total and average using methods, and assigns a grade based on the average. Validate that marks are between 0 and 100.

exercises.title: Debug String Comparison
exercises.description: Identify and correct an incorrect String comparison.
exercises.instructions: Review this code: String a = new String("Java"); String b = new String("Java"); if (a == b) System.out.println("Same"); Explain why the condition is false and rewrite it using equals() to compare content.
